messages:
maria: Customer (ACME) hit installer failures on their Private/VPC deployment. Models fail to download and telemetry events never show up. They say they use a strict egress allowlist through a NAT gateway + stateful FW. They pasted a curl timeout and a dig result.

maria: (customer paste)
> curl -v https://registry.redwood-inference.com/v1/models/foo -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
> * About to connect() to registry.redwood-inference.com port 443 (#0)
> * connect() timed out
> * Closing connection 0

maria: customer also ran:
> dig registry.redwood-inference.com +short
> 10.10.2.5
> (they suspect split-horizon or internal resolver returning non-routable IPs)

sam_infra: Which region/installer version? Are they routing egress through a corporate proxy or pure NAT?

maria: us-west-2, installer v0.8.4. They confirmed no HTTP proxy - egress goes via NAT GW -> corporate FW that only allows specific hosts/ips.

kevin_runtime: Key checklist for model pulls + telemetry: allow SNI passthrough and these hostnames (443 TCP):
- registry.redwood-inference.com (model registry API)
- objects.redwood-inference.com (model shards / CDN)
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com (event ingestion)
- auth.redwood-inference.com (token service)
- packages.redwood-inference.com (installer deps)
- pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org (python deps)
- registry-ctl.redwood-inference.com (health & auth callbacks)
Note: we use CDN fronted hosts for shards so IPs can be ephemeral -> prefer FQDN allowlist + TLS SNI.

kevin_runtime: Quick repro checks to ask them to run from a host behind the same NAT:
- dig + short: dig registry.redwood-inference.com +short
- curl verbose: curl -vI https://registry.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
- openssl: openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername registry.redwood-inference.com < /dev/null
Look for: SNI in ServerName, cert chain, and whether connection completes. If openssl hangs or gets non-routed IP, that's DNS/NAT issue.

jules_sec: Add security notes: we require standard public CA chains (no client certs for pulls), TLS 1.2+ and common ciphers. Many customers with TLS-inspecting proxies break OCSP/Stapling which causes our client to fail during handshake if the proxy doesn't forward proper cert chain. If they have TLS MITM, ask them to whitelist the upstream hostnames rather than intercept.

sam_infra: Minimal allowlist snippet (send to customer's infra team):
- registry.redwood-inference.com:443
- objects.redwood-inference.com:443
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com:443
- auth.redwood-inference.com:443
- packages.redwood-inference.com:443
- pypi.org:443, files.pythonhosted.org:443
Notes: allow DNS resolution to public resolvers for those names; ensure NAT/GW translates to public egress addresses (no hairpin to private 10.x ranges). If they must allow IPs, we can provide published IP ranges for a short window but these change (CDNs).

maria: Customer asked if we can provide a temporary IP list for firewall policy.

kevin_runtime: We can provide short-lived CIDR blocks for the control plane endpoints: 3.112.45.0/24, 52.14.200.0/24 (example) but emphasize these are not permanent for objects CDN. Best practice: allow by FQDN on 443.

infra-bot: automated note: "Published control-plane CIDRs updated 2024-09-03 — check https://redwood-inference.com/ips for canonical list"

jules_sec: Also check OCSP/responder reachability: allow outbound 80/443 to ocsp.* domains if their proxy requires it. If they run an internal resolver returning RFC1918 for our hostnames (split-horizon), they must ensure those IPs are reachable from the installer nodes or change resolver to public for these names.

maria: I'll send recommended host list + the curl/openssl commands to customer and request their dig/curl outputs. I'll ask them to run from an instance in the same subnet as the installer so we avoid NAT variations.

sam_infra: If they still see 10.x addresses from dig, confirm the VPC DHCP options or internal DNS (Route53 private zones) — sometimes enterprises create private zones that shadow public names. If that's intentional, they must route those 10.x addresses to the service via VPN/peer, otherwise our installer can't reach them.

maria: thanks — will follow up. tagging kevin_runtime and jules_sec for visibility :thumbsup:

kevin_runtime: One more tip to give them: run TCP traceroute to the resolved IP to see where the drop happens (tcptraceroute or hping3). Also check iptables/output policy on nodes (MASQUERADE needed for NAT GW flows).

maria: marking for follow-up, will post customer outputs in this thread when available.
